messages:
henry: Heads-up — PaperWave reporting repeated 504s on /v1/generate since 2026-03-18 09:01 UTC. Support ticket: https://support.redwood/paperwave/12345. Example req_id rq_0a3f9c. p95 ~4-6s, tail ~18s. Any quick mitigation?
sofia: grabbing traces & logs now. Do we have gateway request/response headers for rq_0a3f9c? :eyes:
mike: oncall here. Found gateway log for rq_0a3f9c — gateway returned 504 after backend deadline. Backend shows dequeue wait spikes. continuous_batcher.queue_depth peaked ~500 (limit 512), dequeue latency >10s. KV cache churn spikes at same time.
devon: that tenant is sending long-seq streaming requests with slightly different prefixes -> KV cache keeps rebuilding. Continuous batcher holds many inflight, then tail requests time out. We've seen this pattern with long-seq tenants.
henry: I pasted a sample payload in the ticket. Repro curl (staging):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"<very long context>...","max_tokens":1500}'
```
sofia: I can repro the timeout against a hosted replica with that payload. Steps: repeated identical requests -> backlog grows, later requests 504.
mike: quick mitigations: 1) apply per-tenant enqueue cap (do not allow >200 queued requests) 2) route tenant to lower-throughput model variant with tighter seq limits 3) temporarily increase continuous_batcher.dequeue_timeout to avoid 504s while we drain (careful, may increase concurrency). I'll try 1) first.
devon: note: increasing dequeue_timeout is bandaid — underlying problem is KV-cache rebuild on slightly different prompts. Longer-term, we should reuse KV-init for similar prefixes and avoid per-request heavy setup.
sofia: For support reply: asked customer to reduce max_tokens and stop parallelizing large streaming requests. Also requested request_ids and timestamp range. Henry, can you message them the workaround?
henry: pinged customer with workaround & asked for throttling window.
mike: applying per-tenant enqueue cap now (ops command):
```
# run on gateway control plane (ops only)
redwoodctl tenant throttle set --tenant paperwave --enqueue-cap 200 --reason "urgent tail-latency mitigation"
```
mike: monitoring continuous_batcher.backlog and gateway. If backlog drops and tail stabilizes, we keep cap for 24h. :thumbsup:
opsbot: INFO — change applied by mike at 2026-03-18T09:12:21Z.
devon: also putting a small canary patch that shares KV-init between requests with near-identical prefixes to reduce cache rebuilds. Deploying to canary pool.
sofia: any perf numbers from canary?
devon: canary shows 70% reduction in KV build time for those flows and backlog dropped ~60% on the canary nodes after patch. Rolling to more nodes after validation. :shipit:
mike: customer updated — initial improvement after throttling and support guidance, some 504s still early but tail p99 reduced from 18s -> 6s. Continuing to monitor.
henry: will update support ticket and schedule a follow-up call with PaperWave for next week.
sofia: filing short incident writeup + runbook pointer. Runbook added: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/queue-tail-mitigation
devon: followup action items: (1) implement shared KV-init fallback (PR opened) (2) add per-tenant enqueue alerts when >70% of queue cap sustained for 5m (3) review default batcher queue_depth limits for hosted multi-tenant pools.
mike: thanks team. leaving monitoring for next 2 hours then handoff to next oncall.
opsbot: NOTE — incident tagged as "customer-impacting" and assigned to oncall-mike.
sofia: adding :memo: postmortem draft to docs once we confirm root cause.
